p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The relentless march of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) into professional domains has triggered a paradigm shift in global labor dynamics, moving far beyond the automation of routine manual tasks. Historically, technological disruptions primarily displaced blue-collar labor; however, contemporary cognitive computing aggressively targets the white-collar vanguard, executing sophisticated data synthesis, legal document drafting, and algorithmic financial analysis with disconcerting efficacy. While techno-optimists champion this transition as a liberation of human intellect—arguing that AI will subsume mundane analytical friction and elevate workers to higher-tier strategic roles—the velocity of this displacement threatens to outpace systemic re-skilling frameworks. This temporal mismatch risks exacerbating socioeconomic bifurcation, creating a precarious class of highly educated yet functionally obsolete professionals. Furthermore, the corporate imperative to optimize profit margins via algorithmic labor introduces a profound ethical vacuum regarding worker agency and institutional accountability. The ultimate challenge lies not in halting algorithmic integration, but in architecting proactive social safety nets and dynamic educational curricula that treat human capital not as a static resource, but as an adaptable partner to cognitive machines.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: The rapid expansion of Electric Vehicles (EVs) has significantly altered the global transportation landscape. Governments worldwide have promoted EV adoption through subsidies, tax exemptions, and investments in charging infrastructure to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and lower urban pollution levels. Supporters argue that EVs represent a sustainable alternative to conventional automobiles because they produce fewer direct emissions. However, environmental analysts caution that the overall ecological benefit of EVs depends largely on the energy sources used for electricity generation. In nations where coal-fired power plants dominate energy production, EVs may indirectly contribute to substantial carbon emissions. Furthermore, the extraction of rare earth minerals and disposal of lithium-ion batteries raise serious environmental and ethical concerns. Despite these criticisms, technological advancements in battery efficiency and renewable energy integration continue to strengthen the long-term prospects of EVs. Economists also note that the EV industry has created new opportunities for innovation, employment, and industrial investment. Consequently, the debate surrounding EVs is no longer limited to transportation alone but extends to broader questions of sustainability, energy policy, and economic transition.

questions.q: The author's main concern about the “velocity of this displacement” is that
opts: it will end human strategic decision-making
workers will refuse to learn AI tools
re-skilling programmes cannot keep pace with AI adoption
blue-collar workers will be pushed into white-collar roles
questions.why: Displacement “threatens to outpace systemic re-skilling frameworks”. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: “Socioeconomic bifurcation” implies that AI could
opts: split society into two unequal economic segments
questions.why: Bifurcation means splitting in two. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Techno-optimists see AI as a way to
opts: relieve workers of routine cognitive tasks so they can focus on strategy
questions.why: Third sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Which statement is TRUE according to the passage?
opts: Past disruptions hit white-collar workers more
The corporate drive for algorithmic labour raises ethical concerns about worker agency and accountability
The author wants AI integration stopped
Generative AI cannot draft legal documents
questions.why: Fifth sentence; the others contradict the text. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The author's tone toward the future of human labour is best described as
opts: cautionary yet focused on structural adaptation
questions.why: It warns of risks and proposes safety nets and new curricula. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Which of the following best captures the central argument of the passage?
opts: EVs are entirely free from environmental concerns.
EV adoption involves both significant benefits and complex challenges.
Coal-based power generation should be expanded.
questions.why: Main idea: a balanced 'benefits and challenges' option. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Professor in Livestock Production and Management), May 2026.

questions.q: The author implies that the environmental success of EVs depends primarily on:
opts: The nature of electricity production systems
questions.why: Inference: 'depends largely on the energy sources used for electricity generation'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Professor in Livestock Production and Management), May 2026.

questions.q: Why does the author mention "rare earth minerals" and "lithium-ion batteries"?
opts: To note technical limits unrelated to environment
To present environmental and ethical concerns of EV production
questions.why: Purpose question: they 'raise serious environmental and ethical concerns'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Professor in Livestock Production and Management), May 2026.

questions.q: Which of the following can be logically inferred from the passage?
opts: EVs eliminate carbon emissions in all countries.
Renewable energy integration may improve the sustainability of EVs.
questions.why: Inference: 'renewable energy integration continue[s] to strengthen the long-term prospects'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Professor in Livestock Production and Management), May 2026.

questions.q: The tone of the passage may best be described as:
questions.why: Tone: weighs supporters and critics. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Professor in Livestock Production and Management), May 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct modal: “You ______ have told me earlier; I could have helped.”
questions.why: 'Should have' + past participle expresses a past action that was advisable but not done. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Identify the clause type: “The nurse who attended me was very kind.”
questions.why: 'Who attended me' describes the noun 'nurse'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct modal: “The form is optional; you ______ fill it in.”
questions.why: 'Need not' = no obligation; 'must not' = prohibition. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct transformation of: “He is too proud to apologise.”
opts: He is very proud and he apologises.
He is proud enough to apologise.
He is so proud that he will not apologise.
He is so proud that he will apologise.
questions.why: too … to = so … that … not. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: “Hardly had the meeting begun ______ the power failed.”
questions.why: 'Hardly/Scarcely … when'; 'No sooner … than'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

Who won the Golden Glove at the 2026 FIFA World Cup?

questions.q: Under VB-G RAM G, which replaced MGNREGA in 2026, each rural household is guaranteed how many days of wage work a year?
questions.why: MGNREGA guaranteed 100 days.

questions.q: Smriti Mandhana scored 124 off 64 balls in the 2026 Women's T20 Asia Cup against:
PM-KISAN was continued for 2026-27 to 2030-31 with an outlay of about:
questions.why: PM-KISAN gives ₹6,000 a year to farmer families. Aug 2026.

questions.q: The GOBARdhan scheme (₹23,731 crore, FY27–FY36) aims to raise tenfold the production of:
PM Surya Sarovar Yojana (2026) targets 5,000 MW of:
questions.why: With 10,000 MWh of storage. Aug 2026.

questions.q: Ahmedabad hosted, for the first time, a leg of the World Para Series in which sport (2026)?
questions.why: Hyundai World Archery Para Series. Sep 2026.

questions.q: Two trains P and Q start at the same time from X and Y towards each other. After meeting, P takes 4 hours to reach Y and Q takes 9 hours to reach X. If P runs at 72 km/h, what is the distance XY?
questions.why: Speeds are in the ratio √9 : √4 = 3 : 2, so Q = 48 km/h. They meet after √(4 × 9) = 6 h; P travels 6 + 4 = 10 h × 72 = 720 km. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2026.

questions.q: At what time between 3 and 4 o’clock will the hands of a clock be at right angles (after 3:00)?
questions.why: 5.5M − 90 = 90, so M = 32 8/11: about 3:32. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2026.

questions.q: All X are Y. Some Y are Z. No Z is X. Which is true?
questions.why: 'No Z is X' turns round to 'No X is Z'. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2026.

questions.q: April has 30 days. The ratio of rainy days to sunny days in April could NOT be
questions.why: 5 : 3 needs 8 parts; 30 is not a multiple of 8. The others split 30 exactly. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2025.

questions.q: agnoscrenia = poisonous spider; delanocrenia = poisonous snake; agnosdeery = brown spider. Which word could mean "black widow spider"?
questions.why: agnos = spider and comes first; the new word must start with agnos and use no known word. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: A, B and C can do a work in 20, 30 and 60 days. In how many days can A do it if B and C help him every third day?
questions.why: Per 3 days: 3/20 + 1/30 + 1/60 = 12/60 = 1/5 of the work, so 15 days. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2025.

questions.q: Rainfall in the catchment was below normal for two months, yet the city's water supply has not been cut. Assumptions: I. Rainfall later in the monsoon may be adequate. II. Present lake levels may be adequate for normal supply.
opts: Either I or II is implicit
questions.why: Not cutting supply assumes enough water now and the hope of more later. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: Gauri bought things worth ₹25, of which 30 paise was sales tax at 6% on taxable items. What was the cost of the tax-free items?
questions.why: Taxable items: 0.30 ÷ 0.06 = ₹5. Tax-free = 25 − 5 − 0.30 = ₹19.70. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2024.

questions.q: The banker's gain on a sum due 2 years hence at 10% a year is ₹24. What is the present worth?
questions.why: BG = TD × RT/100, so TD = 24 × 100 ÷ 20 = 120; PW = TD × 100 ÷ RT = 600. GPSC CBRT, Apr 2024.

questions.q: Two trains run in opposite directions with speeds 2 : 1. The first passes a standing man in 5 s, the second in 8 s. How long do they take to cross each other?
questions.why: Lengths 10v and 8v; relative speed 3v; 18v ÷ 3v = 6 s. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2024.

questions.q: In Kent's observations, amelioration first followed by aggravation suggests:
opts: a superficial, palliative remedy, or an incurable patient
a correct remedy in the right potency
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. The remedy has acted only superficially; the deeper state then reasserts itself.

questions.q: Diseases kept up by avoidable noxious influences such as poor diet or bad habits, which disappear when these are corrected, are called by Hahnemann:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Not true miasmatic diseases.

questions.q: In chronic diseases (§259–261) Hahnemann advised the patient to avoid:
opts: medicinal substances in food and drink, such as strong coffee, spices and perfumes
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. They disturb the action of the remedy.

questions.q: Extreme weakness from the heat of the sun, with great debility, inability to digest milk and sensitivity to music, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Natrum carb: worse from summer heat and mental exertion.

questions.q: Sensation of a plug in various parts, sweet taste, and complaints relieved by eating are characteristic of:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Anacardium: the plug sensation, relief from eating, two wills.

questions.q: Cough with exhausting weakness of the chest, so weak that the patient cannot talk, and sweetish expectoration suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Stannum: great weakness of the chest, pains come and go gradually.

questions.q: A hurried, anxious patient whose complaints are better at the seashore and worse in the daytime, who sleeps in the knee-chest position and has a history of gonorrhoea, needs:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Medorrhinum: the main anti-sycotic nosode.

questions.q: The continuous fluxion method of preparing high potencies is associated with:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Fincke's fluxion potencies.

questions.q: Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, a homoeopathic medicine that is not of standard quality as per the HPI is called:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. 'Spurious' means imitation or substituted drugs.

questions.q: The first card repertory, 'Boenninghausen's Slips', was introduced by:
questions.why: Guernsey, 1888.

questions.q: C. M. Boger's approach to repertorisation gave special importance to:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Boger used pathological generals and causation.

questions.q: The substance commonly used to measure glomerular filtration rate precisely is:
questions.why: Inulin is freely filtered and neither reabsorbed nor secreted; PAH measures renal plasma flow.

questions.q: Secretin stimulates the pancreas to secrete juice rich in:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Cholecystokinin stimulates enzyme secretion and gallbladder contraction.

questions.q: Thrombocytopenia is a common laboratory finding in:
questions.why: The platelet count is monitored in dengue.

questions.q: Repair by replacement with fibrous tissue, as after a myocardial infarct, is called:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Cardiac muscle cannot regenerate.

questions.q: Which statement about diabetes is FALSE (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025)?
opts: Acromegaly and Cushing's syndrome can cause diabetes
Most type 2 diabetics die of cardiovascular disease
Type 2 diabetics are more prone to ketoacidosis than type 1
Fasting glucose above 126 mg/dL establishes diabetes
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Type 1 diabetes is the ketosis-prone form.

questions.q: Absence (petit mal) seizures show on EEG:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Treated with ethosuximide or valproate.

questions.q: Haemorrhoids that bleed and protrude like a bunch of grapes, relieved by cold water, with a sense of insecurity of the rectum, suggest:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Aloe: grape-like piles, cold water relieves, unsure sphincter.

questions.q: Abnormal uterine bleeding is classified by FIGO using the acronym:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. PALM (structural: polyp, adenomyosis, leiomyoma, malignancy) and COEIN (non-structural).

questions.q: A pregnant woman should receive tetanus–diphtheria (Td) vaccine as:
opts: two doses (or one booster if vaccinated within the last 3 years)
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Under the UIP.

questions.q: Opacity of the lens of the eye is called:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Commonest cause of treatable blindness.

questions.q: A pathological communication between two epithelial surfaces is called a:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. A sinus is a blind tract.

questions.q: Vital statistics include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Vital events are births, deaths, marriages, divorces and so on.

questions.q: Under the homoeopathy practitioners' code of ethics, a registered practitioner is expected to:
opts: display registration details and practise only in his or her own system
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Practitioners must not cross over into other systems except as allowed by law.

questions.q: Datura poisoning presents with:
opts: convulsions with a bitter almond smell
dry mouth, dilated pupils, flushed skin and delirium
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Anticholinergic syndrome.
